clue.text: Reject rendered without blemish

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for rendered wraps around the blemish

parts.note: to render a service is to do it, so rendered means did
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Something is thrown out because it was not made flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: DID goes around SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject something is to throw it away as unwanted, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Maybe put up stand for a cleaner's equipment

indicators.note: maybe put means the letters could be placed in some other order

explanation.surface: Perhaps raise a stand for a cleaner's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reads as one phrase, but 'put' belongs with 'Maybe' as the signal and 'up stand' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-handled scoop used with a brush to collect sweepings is cleaning kit.

clue.text: Get straight drink served outside alternatively

indicators.note: served outside means the drink is placed around the other piece

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A drink served outdoors helps someone sober up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get straight' hints at sobering up, but means put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a matter in order or resolve it, an idiom.

clue.text: Moderate rating at one point

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A middling score at one point in the season.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-officer sailor in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or ease off, as a storm does, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Caused agitation, the nasty brutes did!

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted and unpleasant, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: The nasty thugs stirred up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset or unsettled people, a past-tense verb synonym.

clue.text: A standstill could make one thousand out-of-date

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
the Roman numeral for a thousand is M
passé is French borrowed into English for old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Being stuck could leave one thousand items obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock with no way forward is a standstill, a synonym.

clue.text: Matter for children

explanation.surface: A subject for the young ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter is a topic under discussion; offspring are one's progeny in legal terms.

clue.text: Peak rates as applied to fliers

indicators.note: as applied suggests the letters are put to work in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Top charges imposed on air travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' suggests airline passengers, but means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Small long-tailed parrots are birds, which fly.

clue.text: Girls scored highest

parts.note: reads as top marks for girls, but means female singers with the top vocal part written for them

explanation.surface: Female pupils came top in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' means written in a musical score, not marked in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Italian term for the highest female voice part in a choir.

clue.text: Time for dealing with irregularities

explanation.surface: When to sort out the rough patches.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the day before night; also smoothing things out so they are level.

clue.text: Not quite convinced father's direction is better

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: convinced means sure
pa is father, and the possessive adds S
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone half-persuaded that their dad's way is superior.
explanation.definitionFit: To better a rival is to outdo or exceed them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stick at very light weight

explanation.surface: Clinging on despite carrying very little.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick at something is to hesitate over it on moral grounds; also an old apothecaries' unit of twenty grains.

clue.text: Penny and Rose appealing for wage

parts.note: cute means attractive or appealing

explanation.surface: Penny and Rose making a charming plea for their pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wage' looks like a noun for pay, but it is the verb, as in waging a war.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage a war or campaign is to carry it on, which is to pursue it vigorously.

clue.text: Though drab, the colour is uniform

definitions.text: Though drab, the colour is uniform

parts.words: Though drab, the colour is uniform
parts.note: a dull brownish-yellow shade that also names the soldier's field dress made from cloth of that colour

explanation.surface: A dull shade that is nonetheless consistent throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' reads as consistent, but it means military dress, the cloth named after its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The dull earthy shade is also the cloth used for army service dress.

clue.text: Royalty can revert to salt

indicators.note: to revert is to go back, so the joined words are read from the end to the start

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so for royalty
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: The monarchy might go back to being seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate is a chemical salt, the saltpetre used in gunpowder.

clue.text: Watches exercise when there's a problem in sight

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Watching a workout when a difficulty looms.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching vision is a problem with one's sight.

clue.text: On edge, as the German is in flat

indicators.note: is in places the German article within the word for flat

parts.note: flat in the sense of dull and uninteresting gives boring
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German is nervous while living in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is not a home but dull, and 'On edge' means adjoining rather than nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordering on something is being at the edge of it, adjacent.

clue.text: Cut in — courted disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A bold intervention went badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrease in amount is a cut, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Served in advance, so it's assumed

parts.note: pre- is the prefix for before or in advance
to tend customers is to serve them

explanation.surface: Food served ahead of time, so it is taken for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigned or put on, as an assumed air is a false one.

clue.text: Quiet, like the prudent man's going

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
as means like
a sage is a wise, prudent man

explanation.surface: A wise man departs silently.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey or crossing, the act of travelling.

clue.text: Swell supplement!

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising an extra section of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase in size like a balloon; also to add to or expand a document.

clue.text: Bears buckler and sword

indicators.note: something that buckles bends out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A knight carries a small shield and a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckler' poses as the small round shield of the surface but works as something that buckles, mangling BEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry weapon with a curved blade is a kind of sword.

clue.text: "Coming clean" — article by scholar

indicators.note: by means next to, so the scholar stands beside the article

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: A confession written up by an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming clean' suggests confessing, but means getting washed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a bath is getting oneself washed.

clue.text: Note no quirky talk upset this Greek character

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the words are read bottom to top

parts.note: a lisp is an oddity of speech

explanation.surface: A remark about a speech impediment upsets a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NO and LISP together, making PSILON after E.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet is a Greek letter.

clue.text: Divide the port

explanation.surface: Sharing out the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide is to break into parts; also a harbour city on Croatia's Dalmatian coast.

clue.text: Cuts one in fifty classes

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the others

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
rates as in first-rate, second-rate: grades or classes
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Lessons reduced to one in fifty sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash flesh, a stronger form of cutting.

clue.text: A better bed?

explanation.surface: Is there a superior place to sleep?
explanation.definitionFit: One who lays a wager is a gambler; a stratum of rock or soil is a bed.

clue.text: A rule some people are ignoring

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A regulation that some folk disregard.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of sovereignty is a rule.

clue.text: Heartless rogue taken in by a woman before now

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the following words

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A con man without feeling is fooled by a woman earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by this time has happened previously, an adverb synonym.

clue.text: In it state and sovereign are first

parts.note: taken as written
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: The nation and its monarch come at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a British gold coin worth one pound, so it gives L, the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening letter or stage of something is its earliest, first position.

clue.text: The queen with only one real fault

indicators.note: a fault in rock is a fracture, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch with just a single genuine flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine was queen of France and then England.

clue.text: Hack in time got into shape

indicators.note: in places the horse inside the time of day

parts.note: noon is a time of day
a hack is a hired or worn-out horse, as is a nag

explanation.surface: A hack writer got fit just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' is not a writer but a horse; 'got into' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygon with nine sides is a geometric figure.
